about: Answer-quality test set for CodeWise's own backend (run with --root pointing at this repo). These seed questions were written while building the feature, so they are biased toward what the author knows works. Replace or extend them with real questions: run the server with CODEWISE_QUESTION_LOG=logs/questions.jsonl, then `python eval/draft_from_log.py` and review the draft.

questions.question: How are Python files split into chunks?
questions.reference_answer: Python files are parsed with the ast module; top-level functions and classes become segments (decorators and comments above them included), large classes are split per method, small segments are packed up to max_chars and oversized ones split into overlapping line windows.

questions.question: Who calls replace_file?
questions.reference_answer: CodeWise._ingest in codewise/service.py calls self.index.replace_file after chunking a file.

questions.question: What happens to the old chunks when the same file is uploaded again?
questions.reference_answer: ProjectIndex.replace_file deletes all chunks whose metadata filename matches the path before adding the new chunks, and invalidates the BM25 cache.

questions.question: How are vector search and keyword search results combined?
questions.reference_answer: hybrid_retrieve runs vector search (filtered by max_distance) and BM25 keyword search (with a relative cutoff), optionally graph locations and files named in the question, then fuses the ranked lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (1/(60+rank)).

questions.question: How does the backend make sure the prompt fits in the model's context window?
questions.reference_answer: prepare_question computes an available token budget from num_ctx minus the answer reserve, system prompt and question; code context gets ~70% (minus the relationships section) and history the rest, using estimate_tokens; num_ctx is also passed to Ollama explicitly.

questions.question: Can a client inject a system message through the chat history?
questions.reference_answer: No. sanitize_history keeps only user and assistant roles with string content and drops leading assistant messages.

questions.question: How are zip uploads protected against zip bombs and path traversal?
questions.reference_answer: read_zip limits entry count, per-file and total uncompressed size, reads at most max_file_bytes+1 per entry, skips symlinks, and normalises paths to strip absolute paths and '..'.

questions.question: Which URLs does the GitHub import accept?
questions.reference_answer: parse_github_url accepts only github.com owner/repo URLs (optionally .git or /tree/<ref>) or 'owner/repo'; downloads go to api.github.com and redirects are only allowed to api.github.com or codeload.github.com.

questions.question: How are function calls in Python files found for the code graph?
questions.reference_answer: _python_graph walks the AST with a scope stack; each ast.Call records the called name (Name.id or Attribute.attr), line, enclosing qualname as caller, and the unparsed expression.

questions.question: Which files import store.py?
questions.reference_answer: codewise/app.py imports ProjectStore from codewise/store.py (the service receives the store as a constructor argument).

questions.question: What HTTP status does the upload endpoint return when only some files are indexed?
questions.reference_answer: 207 for partial success; 200 if all were indexed and 400 if none were.

questions.question: How does CodeWise authenticate users with OAuth?
questions.reference_answer: It doesn't: there is no authentication in the uploaded code, and the answer should say so rather than invent one.
